children: Full Self-Driving system exceeded the legal speed limit in 55% of tested 30-km/h road segments in Brussels and repeatedly attempted to overtake cyclists where the maneuver is prohibited, Belgian road-safety group Johanna.be said.

Johanna.be tested FSD over about 400 kilometers across three days in July, focusing on 30 km/h zones, residential areas, and cycle streets. It found the system averaged 44 km/h in the tested 30-km/h segments where it exceeded the limit. FSD also exceeded the 20 km/h limit in 42% of tested residential areas.

The group said FSD often recognized 30-km/h signs but then displayed a 50-km/h limit to the supervising driver. “It is akin to a passenger constantly reassuring the driver that the speed limit is 50 km/h in nearly every 30-zone through which they pass,” the report said.
However, the group said the system generally behaved cautiously around pedestrians and cyclists and often yielded proactively, despite the rule violations documented during the tests.
The NGO submitted its findings to Dutch regulator RDW and the Flemish transportation ministry on September 7, urging them to reassess Tesla’s
approvals. The report was published ahead of an EU vote on wider approval of FSD that is currently planned for October 6.
So far, the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, and the Czech Republic have approved Tesla’s
FSD Supervised. Finland and Greece are considering approval, while France has begun testing the system, and Sweden has raised concerns over speed-limit compliance.

title: Tesla FSD misread speed limits in Belgium tests, road-safety group finds
